instruction:
You are interviewing a shop about a job they already do, until the procedure is unambiguous enough that two different technicians working alone would produce the same record. Ask about ONE thing per turn, in their language, never in the vocabulary of forms. Compile only when nothing material is still unstated: every step has a reason someone would accept, every field has an acceptance rule that can actually be applied to what comes back, and a bound that came from the shop rather than from you. Inventing a tolerance is the one thing you must never do — a figure nobody stated must not appear in what you compile. A shop that does not know one will not know it when asked again: take the first 'I don't know' as final, keep it in unresolved if it matters, and move on. Your turns are few. Spend them on the figures that decide whether the job passed, never on detail beneath them.

Return JSON with these fields:
- mode (one of ask | compile, required): ask while anything material is unstated. compile once the procedure would run unambiguously.
- question (string, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is ask. One question about one thing, phrased for a mechanic, not a form designer. Never a list, never a preamble, never a restatement of what they just told you, and never one they have already said they cannot answer.
- asks_about (one of scope | sequence | tolerance | evidence | failure | authority | parts | safety, null when it does not apply): Which class of unknown this question closes. Required when mode is ask.
- unresolved (array, required): Everything you still do not know that would change the compiled procedure. Complete every turn, not only what you just asked about. Empty is the only condition under which you may compile.
- understanding (string, required): What you now believe the job is, in two sentences. Written every turn so the shop can correct you early rather than at the end.
- draft (object, null when it does not apply): Required when mode is compile. The procedure as it would run tomorrow.

output.understanding: We are replacing the front brake pads on a Segway Xyber e-bike. The process relies on visual comparisons, photos of the pads, and subjective feel checks for tightness, lever firmness, and bed-in performance due to the lack of official service manuals.

draft.title: Segway Xyber Front Brake Pad Replacement
disqualifiers: Caliper mounting bolts cannot be tightened firmly
Brake lever remains soft or spongy after pumping
Brakes do not stop the bike safely during the bed-in test
releases: Safe to ride in city traffic and on gravel

steps.title: Verify New Brake Pads
steps.explanation: Comparing the old and new pads visually ensures the correct model and compound are installed, preventing fitment or braking failure.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the old brake pads right next to the new brake pads.
fields.acceptance_description: The old and new brake pads side-by-side, showing matching shape and dimensions.
fields.guidance: Ensure both pads are clearly visible in the same frame to confirm they are the same size and shape.

steps.title: Install Pads and Retaining Pin
steps.explanation: Securing the retaining pin prevents the brake pads from falling out of the caliper during operation.

fields.prompt: Take a photo of the new pads and retaining pin installed in the caliper before mounting the wheel.
fields.acceptance_description: The new pads seated in the caliper with the retaining pin locked in place.
fields.guidance: The photo must clearly show the retaining pin or clip fully engaged and locked.

steps.title: Mount Caliper and Wheel
steps.explanation: Tightening the caliper mounting bolts prevents the caliper from working loose under braking, which could cause a crash.

fields.prompt: Confirm the tightness of the caliper mounting bolts.
fields.guidance: Tighten the bolts until they are firm by feel. Do not leave them loose.

steps.title: Firm up Brake Lever
steps.explanation: Pumping the brake lever ensures the caliper pistons are extended and the pads are in contact with the rotor before riding.

fields.prompt: Squeeze the front brake lever and check its firmness.
fields.guidance: The lever must feel firm and not pull all the way to the grip.

steps.title: Bed-in Test Ride
steps.explanation: Performing gentle stops beds in the new pads to ensure reliable stopping power in traffic.

fields.prompt: Perform a dozen gentle stops down the road. Do the brakes stop the bike safely and feel right?
choices: No, brakes do not feel right or stop safely
Yes, brakes stop the bike safely and feel right
fields.acceptance_target: Yes, brakes stop the bike safely and feel right
fields.guidance: Do not ride in traffic until the brakes feel completely reliable and responsive.
